extracted.intended_audience: DoD managers, contracting officers, financial managers, and researchers analyzing OMB Circular A-76 and Defense Working Capital Fund (DWCF) competition studies
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for conducting OMB Circular A-76 cost-comparison studies and for operating/evaluating Defense Working Capital Fund activities (including a NAVSISA case study). Focuses on cost comparison rules, DWCF business model and ABC costing, appeals, transition, and post-selection reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective of the cost comparison
rubrics_metrics.description: The objective of the cost comparison is to ensure that the two proposals provide the same scope of work and level of performance and bases the final selection on lowest cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates a tentative decision to accept either the in-house MEO or the contractor external bid; if the Government in-house proposal is deficient there is a revision to ensure a fair comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum cost differential requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a minimum cost differential requirement: the contractor proposal must be 10% lower than the Government proposal or $10M less over the performance period, whichever is less.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the contractor proposal is above the threshold, the function remains in the government. The minimum cost differential requirement is to account for the cost of conversion to a private contractor when there is only a small savings realized. Upon passing the threshold test, the Contracting Officer informs the Unit Commander of the tentative decision to prepare for the official announcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative Appeals filing requirements and eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeals to the A-76 steps must be in writing and received by the contracting officer within the review period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The contractor submitting the appeal has to have submitted a proposal for bid. Federal employees or government agencies eligible for replacement by outsourcing may also submit an appeal. Overall, the cost comparison is the most frequent point or issue of appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transition Plan (TP) content and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Administrative Appeal process is completed the final selectee, whether the government in-house MEO or contractor, begins the Transition Plan (TP).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The TP will address the personnel management issues, transfer of equipment and inventories, and any procedural changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-MEO Performance Review requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If the organization implements the MEO, the organization conducts a formal review and inspection following the end of the first full year of performance (Post-MEO Performance Review).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The review confirms that the MEO has been implemented in accordance with the Transition Plan, establishes the MEO ability to perform the services of the PWS, and confirms that actual costs are within the estimates contained in the in-house estimate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post A-76 QASP implementation and review
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon completion of the A-76, the new organization begins full performance and the Government implements the QASP regardless of the final choice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The organization reviews the QASP periodically to ensure the validity of the PWS set by the A-76. In the case where the organization implements the Government MEO, a formal review and inspection of the MEO occurs at the end of the first year of operation to verify compliance with the Government Management plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: How effectiveness/savings are measured in A-76 studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Savings demonstrated by A-76 studies are shown via reductions in Civil Service Full Time Equivalent (FTE) employees and corresponding dollar savings and percent of total budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data tables and service-level breakdowns (e.g., number of studies completed, FTE reduced, savings in $ and percent) are used to report effectiveness; note that reported savings may reflect personnel savings rather than operational savings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required elements to qualify as a Working Capital Operation (WCF)
rubrics_metrics.description: There are three required elements for an organization to qualify as a Working Capital Operation: (1) an identifiable product or service, (2) customers that will buy the product or service, (3) a cost accounting system to provide total cost visibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These elements distinguish WCF activities from other DoD organizations and are foundational to adopting DWCF business practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supply Management vs Non-Supply Management distinction
rubrics_metrics.description: DoD organizes WCF into Supply Management (Stock Fund) and non-Supply Management (Industrial) areas; the major difference is that Supply Management operations receive contract authority permitting obligations in advance of customer orders while non-supply areas must have immediate budgetary resources in the form of customer orders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-supply actual outlay may not occur until a future date but resources must be available; this affects cash flow, pricing, and rate stabilization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Activity Group classification for WCF organization
rubrics_metrics.description: WCFs are placed into Activity Groups (Supply Management, Depot Maintenance, Research and Development, Transportation, Information Services, Public Works, Financial Operations, Distribution Depots, Defense Commissary Agency, Other).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some Activity Groups are unique to each service, others cross services or are Defense-wide; all DoD components have Supply Management and Depot Maintenance groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: DWCF foundational strategy and objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: The DWCF is a financial strategy that engages competition and establishes customer/provider relations, adopts private-sector techniques, consolidates functions, and uses activity-based accounting to display full costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary goal: manage 'total cost' of delivery and recover all costs on a break-even basis over time; advantages listed include identifying true costs to Congress and users, underlining cost consequences, providing managers financial authority/flexibility, improving cost estimates/control, placing customers in position to evaluate price/quality, allowing flexibility (no fiscal-year limits), and establishing stabilized unit prices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benefits expected from introducing competition (A-76 rationale)
rubrics_metrics.description: The A-76 process creates savings by introducing competition, striving for economy and enhanced productivity, and forcing organizations to self-evaluate and improve efficiency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Competition compels both Government and industry to become more efficient; A-76 is intended to keep inherently governmental functions in-house while relying on commercial sector where more economical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Activity Based Costing (ABC) principle in WCF
rubrics_metrics.description: WCF managers use Activity Based Costing to capture and allocate costs across a product; unit cost is defined as costs divided by measurement of output (cost driver).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of cost drivers: Direct Labor Hours (DLH) or units of goods sold. In ABC, the providing activity influences the numerator (costs) while the customer influences the denominator (output measure). Managers use ABC to determine unit cost and make decisions on labor/materials to produce better products/services at competitive rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost element definitions for WCF accounting
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost elements include Direct Costs, Indirect Costs, General and Administration (G&A), Variable Costs, and Fixed Costs, each defined for allocation and pricing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct costs are directly attributable and allocated over individual units; Indirect costs are allocated across outputs (overhead); G&A are overall operating overhead; Variable costs change with workload (e.g., labor/materials); Fixed costs remain the same across operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rate-setting and Billable Work Years/Billable Hours methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Example NAVSISA rate formula: Rate = (All Labor + Non-labor - (Profit + Loss)) / (Billable Employees x Billable Hours). Billable Hours are computed from total available hours minus leave, holidays, sick, training, etc., yielding a Billable Hours figure (e.g., 1650).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizations must adjust rates for prior year gains or losses to strive for an Accumulated Operating Result (AOR) of zero (breakeven). The numerator carries costs (including overhead and prior year adjustments) while the revenue denominator is limited to revenue-generating employees/hours, creating pressure to minimize labor costs and maximize billable hours.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniqueness/market-availability criterion for WCF activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Some DWCF functions are unique to DoD (e.g., Depot Maintenance, R&D) and may lack private-market demand, resulting in de facto monopoly; most DWCF areas, however, produce similar products to the commercial sector and face open competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where private-sector equivalents exist, open market competition should be used; where uniqueness exists, competition may be limited and A-76 applicability differs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation: A-76 is a cost-comparison tool only
rubrics_metrics.description: The A-76 is evaluating organizations based on cost comparison only; the study does not take into consideration the quality of work or timeliness of work completion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explicit limitation: decisions driven solely by cost can omit important performance and quality dimensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness criterion for applying A-76 to WCF activities
rubrics_metrics.description: The A-76 may be inappropriate for Working Capital Fund activities that already operate in a constant state of competition because it is a lengthy, labor-intensive process that provides only a single-point-in-time verification of efficiency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A-76 studies typically take 18–36 months, and the WCF marketplace is dynamic and must frequently change to keep competitive advantage; therefore, alternative or lighter-weight tools may be more suitable for continuously competing WCF activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: OMB Circular decision rule on providing commercial products/services
rubrics_metrics.description: In accordance with OMB Circular provisions, the Government shall not conduct any activity to provide a commercial product or service if the product or service is available more economically from a commercial source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied at NAVSISA: if A-76 shows NAVSISA can be more economically performed by contract forces, decision is to move to a private sector provider which would lower stabilized rates on contract work.
